column3: It exactly restates the focus triad: God is the true, other calls are false, and God is the High, Great.
It adds the distinct pattern of knowingly mixing and concealing truth with falsehood.
It identifies the revealed book as truth from the Lord, supporting the focus's claim of divine reality.
It repeats that God is the true and grounds this in giving life and power over all things.
Its nearby description of believers' practice and certainty gives only broad context within the surah.
Cosmic alternation and exclusive dominion show why those called besides God possess nothing.
It directly contrasts God's judgment by truth with the utter inability of those called besides Him to judge.
It makes the focus's falsehood concrete: other calls can neither benefit nor harm.
It joins divine transcendence to the denial of spouse and child, clarifying non-comparability.
It frames truth and falsehood through the divergent consequences of following each.
The true divine promise gives a nearby surah instance of haqq as dependable fulfillment.
It makes exclusive calling an exclusive worship obligation rather than an abstract assertion.
It locates all alleged calls besides God under His complete knowledge and wisdom.
Its production challenge tests claims by the actual capacity of every supposed helper.
Human self-exaltation offers a limited contrast with the focus's genuinely divine highness.
It closely joins exclusive calling, rejection of association, judgment, and God's being the High, Great.
Its warning against human pride in the same surah contrasts false self-exaltation with God's highness.
It demands evidence that alleged objects of invocation created anything or share celestial dominion.
It specifies falsehood as incapable of initiating or restoring anything when truth arrives.
Wrongly consuming wealth through falsehood does not clarify the focus's theological contrast.
It counters a fabrication charge by affirming revelation as truth from the Lord.
It directly states that truth's arrival exposes falsehood as perishing.
The nearby ethical instruction supplies only general surah context for right and wrong.
It portrays God as establishing truth through His words despite opposition.
It sharply distinguishes the true call from futile appeals that never reach a response.
It depicts truth as actively delivered by the Knower of the unseen against falsehood.
Its closing divine highness is remote from the focus's argument about divine uniqueness.
God's protective authority for believers only broadly supports His exclusive authority.
It gives the surah's explicit refusal of association without knowledge, even under parental pressure.
The challenge to ask the great idol exposes that claimed greatness lacks speech and agency.
It links establishing truth with nullifying falsehood as coordinated divine action.
Divine dominion and the loss of falsehood-makers add a broad eschatological consequence.
Paradisal elevation is not a close account of God's highness or exclusive divinity.
It directly identifies calls besides God as directed to powerless false objects.
The same-surah assertion that God's promise is true reinforces haqq as reliable reality.
Pharaoh's coercive claim to greatness is a secondary contrast with God's true greatness.
It combines permitted intercession, recognition of truth, and God's being the High, Great.
The scale of lesser and greater punishment does not illuminate the focus's three claims.
It addresses inherited association and rejects treating ancestral practice as an excuse.
Divine hearing and knowledge in a statement about changed favor offer only a remote link.
The same-surah conclusion on God's exclusive knowledge provides broad authority context.
It shows how rejection can label divine signs and their bearers as false instead of engaging evidence.
Night and day alternation provides the operative cosmic order that the focus's context invokes.
The comprehensive register of small and great matters does not clarify the focus.
It directly rebukes assigning creatures as partners to their Creator and affirms His transcendence.
Universal possession is explicitly paired with God's being the High, Great.
Revelation sent with truth is a general but redundant support for the focus's haqq.
It intensifies haqq into certainty, adding an epistemic dimension to divine truth.
God's knowledge of unseen and seen is coupled with His greatness and transcendence.
The rejection of God's signs and killing without right only broadly concerns resistance to truth.
Mutual exhortation to truth gives a practical communal response but not the focus's theology.
It presents sole divinity, unrestricted dominion, dependent intercession, knowledge, and divine highness together.
It depicts truth as decisively striking falsehood until it vanishes.
Creation in truth is immediately paired with God's transcendence above their associations.
The great divine bounty is too general to clarify the focus's claims.
The worldly life's play and reward language does not add to the focus.
At judgment, alleged partners deny the associators' claim, exposing the invoked relationship as false.
It joins the true account with the categorical assertion that there is no deity except God.
Divine support and steadfastness provide only a broad consequence of allegiance to God.
It distinguishes arrogant self-raising from legitimate elevation, but only indirectly.
The final recompense reveals God as the manifest true, adding an eschatological disclosure of haqq.
Its account of clear and ambiguous verses offers only a distant interpretive connection to truth.
It shows denial of arriving truth producing confusion, without addressing divine uniqueness.
It calls revelation truth but mainly concerns divisive dispute about the book.
The morning cry narrative does not clarify the focus.
The command to glorify the Most High directly supports the focus's divine highness.
It repeats that calling what neither harms nor benefits is far error.
The inversion and stone rain episode does not illuminate the focus's argument.
It states truth from the Lord but its primary concern is the choice and consequence of belief.
It denies independent possession of intercession to those called besides God and conditions it on truth.
It shows that alleged gods called besides God provide no aid when divine command comes.
The fulfilled requests of paradise are unrelated to calling others besides God.
It pairs erasing falsehood with establishing truth by God's words.
Disputation over God's signs and worldly movement do not add a distinct focus connection.
The messenger's coming with truth is a general, already well-covered affirmation.
It rejects turning from divine guidance to calls that neither benefit nor harm.
The warning not to invalidate deeds only loosely touches the falsehood vocabulary.
Its human military superiority is distinct from the focus's divine highness.
It confronts worship besides God with the ultimate loss it entails.
The vision of a great kingdom in paradise does not clarify God's highness in the focus.
It tersely affirms truth from the Lord but adds no new dimension after earlier parallels.
It denies that those called besides God create anything and stresses that they are created.
Sealing the hearts of those without knowledge offers no distinct aid here.
It names God the true protector after all lesser supports fail.
It rejects treating other protectors as intermediaries for closeness to God and affirms religion as His alone.
It contrasts belief in falsehood with ingratitude for God's favor, only broadly related to the focus.
Iblis's arrogance is a secondary contrast with the focus's divine greatness.
Its uncompromising assertion of God's oneness is the focus's central theological conclusion.
Its parable gives a vivid account of truth remaining useful while falsehood passes away.
The believers' granted requests in the hereafter do not clarify the focus.
The statement that an event contains signs and a test is too general.
It contributes the distinct warning against covering truth with falsehood.
The household etiquette passage does not materially clarify the focus.
It counters a human-authorship explanation, only indirectly related to truth versus falsehood.
Creation and life from water offer broad evidence of divine power, not the focus's specific contrast.
God's knowledge of unseen and seen is followed by His transcendence above all associations.
The social conduct ruling does not contribute to the focus.
Calling arriving truth sorcery illustrates rejection by relabeling, but is a peripheral parallel.
The rescue of Jonah and believers does not clarify the focus's claims.
Rejoicing without right is too remote from the focus's argument.
The immediately preceding sign of God merging night and day and subjecting sun and moon supplies the operative evidence introduced by the focus's therefore.
Luqman's direct warning that association is a grave wrong gives the surah's explicit ethical diagnosis of the error rejected in the focus.
It exposes the contradiction of admitting God created the heavens and earth while still turning elsewhere in worship.
Universal ownership is assigned to God alone, directly supporting the focus's distinction between true sovereignty and false calls.
It asks whether alleged partners created anything and denies that they possess benefit or harm, directly matching the focus's anti-association argument.
Its human analogy about refusing to make dependents equal partners in provision closely parallels the focus's logic against assigning partners to God.
It asks whether any alleged partners can create, provide, cause death, or give life, making the focus's claim of their falsehood concrete.
It denies that alleged deities own even an atom or share any partnership in heaven or earth.
It challenges taking powerless intercessors besides God, extending the focus's rejection of supposedly effective others.
It identifies those worshipped besides God as unable to harm or benefit and rejects their claimed intercessory role.
It contrasts many competing lords with the One, Overpowering God, joining divine oneness and supreme authority.
It restricts judgment and worship to God, directly turning the focus's theology into exclusive allegiance.
It prohibits taking two gods and grounds worship in the fact that God is one.
It denies that those besides God possess provision from heaven or earth or have any power.
It forbids placing another deity alongside God and names the resulting abandonment and blame.
It challenges the supposed alternatives to remove harm or alter it, testing their causal incapacity.
It rebukes taking gods besides God without clear authority, directly joining association to the absence of proof.
It declares that there is no deity except God and affirms His uniquely excellent names.
It identifies God alone as the deity whose knowledge encompasses all things, excluding the calf from divine status.
It argues that multiple gods would have corrupted the heavens and earth, grounding uniqueness in coherent dominion.
It demands proof for taking gods besides God and directs attention to revealed remembrance instead.
It condemns worshipping beside God what lacks both authorization and knowledge, directly exposing baseless association.
It denies that God has a child or any god alongside Him, since competing deities would each claim their creation and dominate one another.
It assigns exclusive dominion and creation to God while explicitly denying that He has any partner in dominion.
It contrasts God with objects taken as gods that create nothing, are created, and control neither harm nor benefit.
It gives the direct command not to invoke another deity with God, reinforcing exclusive worship.
It repeatedly asks whether any god is with God after enumerating creative and providential signs.
It continues the challenge by linking ordered earth, rivers, and mountains to the denial of any god with God.
It tests alleged partners against answering the distressed, removing harm, and granting stewardship on earth.
It asks whether any god is with God in guidance through darkness, winds, and mercy.
It joins originating and restoring creation with provision, then challenges whether any god is with God.
It declares that He is God, that praise and judgment belong to Him, and that there is no deity except Him.
It forbids calling another deity with God and grounds all enduring reality, judgment, and return in Him alone.
It states that those worshipped besides God create nothing and cannot provide, directing seekers of provision back to God.
Its depiction of incapacity to make the deaf hear is only a secondary parallel to the focus's causal contrast.
It presents God as Creator and ruler of the heavens and earth, then denies any protector or intercessor besides Him.
It exposes the claimed partners as objects of misguided worship rather than genuine divine associates.
It asks whether any creator besides God provides from heaven and earth, then declares no deity except Him.
It states that those called besides God cannot hear, cannot answer, and will deny the association on the Day of Resurrection.
It challenges alleged partners to show what they created or share in, exposing the absence of any warrant.
It rejects taking gods besides God because their intercession cannot avail and they cannot rescue from intended harm.
It notes that people take gods besides God hoping for aid, a motive the focus classifies as false.
It opens with the categorical assertion that the deity is one.
It grounds that oneness in lordship over the heavens, earth, and everything between them.
It exposes the contradiction of confessing God as Creator while still calling on others that cannot avert or withhold His decree.
It identifies God as Creator of all things and trustee over all things, supplying the positive basis for exclusive divinity.
It rejects being commanded to worship other than God after the truth of His status has been made clear.
It identifies God as the Creator of all things and declares that there is no deity except Him.
It explicitly prohibits worshipping those invoked besides God after clear proofs have come.
It declares that the deity is one and commands upright devotion to Him alone.
It prohibits worship of sun and moon and commands worship of God who created them.
It exposes the inconsistency of acknowledging God as Creator while turning away from Him.
It calls those who invoke others besides God the most astray because their objects neither answer nor know of the invocation.
It shows that supposed gods taken for nearness to God vanish when aid is needed, proving the claim false.
It commands not to set another deity with God and presents the warning as direct revelation.
It asks whether they have a deity other than God and declares His transcendence above their associations.
It confines the Prophet's invocation to his Lord and rejects associating anyone with Him.
It declares God Lord of east and west and that there is no deity except Him, directing reliance to Him alone.
